reason: The tiny lymph vessels are shown beside cells, where they can collect fluid that leaves blood capillaries.
expectation: The tiny lymph vessels should form the beginning of a route that collects excess fluid around the cells.

effect: The tiny lymph vessels collect fluid between cells while the blood vessel stays separate. The larger vessels look like the next part of the return route.
reaction: It was useful to see where the fluid enters.
reason: The larger lymph vessels collect from smaller vessels and lead toward a vein.
expectation: The larger vessels should carry the collected fluid toward the vein.

effect: The tissue with lymph capillaries cannot currently combine with anything, so I should try building the larger return route separately.
reaction: I was surprised the small and larger vessels did not join directly.
reason: The larger lymph vessel ends beside a vein, and the vein connection picture shows that junction.
expectation: This should connect the larger lymph return vessel to the vein.

effect: The larger lymph vessels now connect to the neck vein, with valves helping fluid move forward. The small-vessel tissue still could not combine earlier, so I will work on the other goal.
reaction: The valve panels make the return route clearer, though the separate small vessels are still puzzling.
reason: The nervous system model has outgoing signals to muscles, so it should connect to the arm assembly.
expectation: The arm should connect to nerves that carry signals between it and the nervous system.

effect: The arm is now connected to nerves carrying information in and muscle signals out. The breathing and circulation apparatus still needs connecting.
reaction: The two-way arrows make the connection clear.
reason: The goal calls for joining nerves and muscles with breathing and blood supply, which the breathing apparatus contains.
expectation: The connected arm and nervous system should join the breathing and blood circulation model.

effect: The arm and nervous system now have a blood supply, and nerves reach the breathing muscles. The fluid-return goal remains.
reaction: The inset helped distinguish nerve signals from supplies carried by blood.
reason: The lymph return route is built, but the earlier attempt to join the small vessels failed. Inspecting it should show what can connect next.
expectation: The compatibility list should show how to finish connecting the fluid-return route.

effect: Inspecting the return route automatically joined it to the lymph capillaries, completing the path to the vein. The new goal is to connect it to the body.
reaction: I was surprised the same pieces could join after the larger route was connected to the vein.
reason: The new goal names the return route and the supplied body, which are now both available.

choice.with: Body with nerves and blood supply

expectation: The lymph drainage network should connect to the body and return excess tissue fluid to its blood.

effect: The lymph network is now connected to the body, completing both goals. The final picture brings together nerve signals, muscle work, blood supply and fluid return.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the separate routes work together in one model.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting the lymph drainage network to the body was most worthwhile because the final picture showed how fluid return fits alongside movement and blood supply.

leastWorthwhile.text: Trying to join the small and larger lymph vessels directly was frustrating: the pieces looked like they should connect, but the attempt gave no explanation of what was missing.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the small vessels could join the larger route only after the latter was connected to a vein.

arbitrary.text: The requirement to connect the larger vessels to the vein before joining the small vessels felt arbitrary; the pictures did not make that order clear.

continue.text: I would probably continue: seeing nerve signals, blood supply and fluid return come together was interesting, although I would hope future prerequisites are clearer.
